To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the skewedness of the gluon distribution leads to a Q^2 dependence for the diffractively produced rho meson cross section that is much steeper than the one obtained from the use of the standard gluon distribution.

the Q^2 evolution of the cross section is consistent with the skewed distribution, that the ratio of the longitudinal and transverse cross sections is consistent with the predictions of perturbative QCD, that the skewed gluon is a good candidate for the diffractively produced gluon, and that the J/psi is a good probe of gluon saturation.
the diffractive rho production cross section is consistent with HERA data at small x, but that the J/psi cross section is too small by about a factor of 10.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of diffractive production in the framework of perturbative QCD.
diffractive vector-meson production in deep inelastic scattering.
the diffractive electroproduction of vector mesons at high energy, in particular the Q^2 evolution of the cross section.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data is consistent with a model in which the diffractive vector production is dominated by a hard process.
the data on the diffractive electroproduction of the rho and J/PSI mesons are in good qualitative agreement with the predictions of our approach.
we are in a good position to make a prediction for the Q^2 behavior of the cross section and the longitudinal-to-transverse ratio for diffractive electroproduction of vector mesons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data on the Q^2-dependence is well explained by the use of the parton distributions in a transverse momentum dependent approach.

the Q^2 evolution of the rho and J/ psi cross sections is consistent with the skewed parton distributions, but the data are not yet precise enough to distinguish between the various skewed distributions.
the skewed distribution gives the correct Q^2 dependence for the data, while the color singlet model gives the correct normalization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of parton-hadronic duality is a very good approximation for diffractive electroproduction of vector mesons.
the skewedness effects are very important for the Q^2 evolution of diffractive cross sections.

diffractive rho production is a good probe of the skewed gluons, and that the skewed gluons are not too small at small x, but the skewed gluons at HERA do not seem to be very different from the standard (collinear) gluon distribution.
